messages.subject: Greetings Wallace Users!
parts:
At its foundation, this is a forum to ask and answer questions about the Wallace Ecological Modeling App, but it is also a space to discuss further collaborative development of the software, discuss topics related to the implementation of ecological modeling in R, and anything else you think is relevant.

Welcome, and please feel free to post any questions you'd like.

messages.author: fcb165f109659066
messages.subject: Re: Greetings Wallace Users!
parts:
Dear Jamie and the Wallace team (nice name :) ).

Congrats for this piece of work. Useful for several members of the broader scientific community but also for Protected Area managers and Policy makers.

I will use it the next days in detail - one question, are more algorithms planned to be incorporated ? Let say, Random Forests and Support Vector Machines ?

Looking forward

Dimitris.

messages.author: fe049c2835236bb1
messages.subject: Re: Greetings Wallace Users!
parts:
Thanks for your interest! We plan to add some more algorithms to the workflow soon, but we haven’t decided which ones. We will keep the group informed when any changes to available algorithms are made, and will consider all suggestions.

Jamie M. Kass
PhD Candidate
City College of NY

messages.author: fcb165f109659066
messages.subject: Re: Greetings Wallace Users!
parts:
Thanks Jamie

If you accept suggestions, focus at Random Forests and Support Vector Machines.
Also, to have option for model evaluation using independent dataset from the training (e.c. when we have data for invasive species from the native area but also from the invaded area).

Looking forward

messages.author: fe049c2835236bb1
messages.subject: Re: Greetings Wallace Users!
parts:
Dimitris,

Thanks for the suggestions. I was wondering why you selected those two algorithms in particular. If you have expertise with these algorithms and their implementation, and especially if you have R functions that work with them, we'd be interested in helping you develop some new modules for Wallace.

As for the independent evaluation, this would be a great addition, and I will add it to the list. Not everyone wants to evaluate by cross-validation, and we want to enable more flexibility for evaluating models.

Jamie Kass
PhD Candidate
City College of New York

messages.author: fcb165f109659066
messages.subject: Re: Greetings Wallace Users!
parts:
Hi Jamie and Wallace community,

These two algorithms are quite robust in over-fitting and require much less data (especially background data for the pseudo-absence). I use them for image classification (remote sensing) and have superior performance in terms of accuracy in comparison to others.

On the R side, am dummy :). I use some code - mostly ready-to-use by colleagues, adapted for my data). Thus, i cannot help on the development but on the use side.

The independent evaluation is very important. especially in invasion ecology (as am working on that) but also in cases that you model a species and use the results for targeted field campaigns for data collection and use of model output for conservation decisions.

I have real world data, so, if you need any help on testing modules on real data (rather on virtual species which i hate) let me know.

D.
